warning_template:
## Warnings

- An AI chatbot (Claude) wrote this fix. No human has reviewed the fix.
- Nobody has run the fix against the project's own test suite.
- Nobody has checked whether someone else already sent a fix for the same bug.
- The fix was written against the project's code as of 9 November 2026 and may no longer apply cleanly.
- Nobody has sent the fix to the project. Anyone is free to test the fix and send the fix.

fixes.title: json-rpc: setting an error on a response leaves the old result in place
fixes.symptom: A JSON-RPC response object that already holds a result keeps the result after code sets an error on the response. The response then carries both a result and an error. The JSON-RPC rules allow only one of the two.
fixes.change: The error setter in jsonrpc1.py and jsonrpc2.py removed a key named value that never exists. The fix removes the key named result and only when the error is set to a real value. A new test named test_error_setter_removes_result covers the case.
fixes.words: JSONRPC20Response JSONRPC10Response error setter result and error both present _data.pop value json-rpc python
fixes.report_title: Response error setter pops 'value' instead of 'result'

fixes.title: mcp-task-app: every task gets the program start time as task_started
fixes.symptom: Every new task shows the same task_started time. The time shown is the moment the program started and not the moment the task was created.
fixes.change: The code called datetime.now() once when the program loaded and reused that one value as the default. The fix passes the function datetime.now to SQLAlchemy and uses Field(default_factory=datetime.now) in the Pydantic model so each task gets a fresh time. No test is included. The project looks like a teaching project so the maintainer may prefer that students fix the bug.
fixes.words: task_started default datetime.now() evaluated once at import SQLAlchemy Column default Pydantic default_factory same timestamp every row
fixes.report_title: [BUG] task_started default is fixed at import time

fixes.title: Gulliver: spend with a huge --days value crashes with OverflowError
fixes.symptom: Running the spend command with a very large --days number such as 10000000 crashes with OverflowError: date value out of range instead of showing a clear message.
fixes.change: The fix wraps the date arithmetic in runaway.py in a try block and returns the error message "--days is too large." with a suggested next step. A new test covers two huge values.
fixes.words: gulliver spend --days OverflowError date value out of range timedelta runaway.py
fixes.report_title: spend: a very large --days crashes with a Python traceback instead of an error message

fixes.title: kraft: update_repo skips the shared response handling
fixes.symptom: The client call update_repo parsed the server reply with code of its own. A reply with status 200 and a body that is not JSON (for example an HTML page from a proxy) slipped through as a fake success. The other client calls report that case as a bad response.
fixes.change: The fix makes update_repo use the shared helpers transport._detail and transport._json in src/kraft/client/actions.py. A new parametrized test case named text-200-patch covers the HTML reply.
fixes.words: kraft client update_repo BAD_RESPONSE non-JSON 200 response proxy html transport._json transport._detail status_error
fixes.report_title: update_repo reports an answer that isn't JSON as success

fixes.title: Gulliver: parse_period with a huge number crashes with OverflowError
fixes.symptom: Giving the period reader a very large number of minutes or hours or days or weeks crashes with OverflowError instead of a clear error.
fixes.change: The fix wraps the timedelta creation in parse_period in src/gulliver/incremental.py and raises ValueError with the message "period is too large". One new test line covers the case.
fixes.words: gulliver parse_period OverflowError timedelta days too large incremental.py period is too large
fixes.report_title: Period values such as `prune --older-than 99999999999d` and `check --fresh ts=99999999999d` crash with a traceback

fixes.title: AgenticResourceRegistry: web screens show the command observal pull which does not exist
fixes.symptom: Five places in the web interface tell people to type observal pull. The real command is observal agent pull. A person who copies the shown command gets an error.
fixes.change: The fix changes the shown text to observal agent pull in preview-panel.tsx and home.tsx and teamspace-detail.tsx and teamspaces.tsx. Text change only. No test is included.
fixes.words: observal pull observal agent pull wrong command in UI No such command registry home teamspaces preview panel

fixes.title: repowise: a heading inside a code fence is treated as a real section heading
fixes.symptom: When a generated page contains a code sample with a line that starts with # or ## the section embedder treats that line as the start of a new section and cuts or replaces the wrong part of the page.
fixes.change: The fix adds a helper named _section_span in overview_tables.py that tracks code fences made of three backticks or three tildes and ignores headings inside fences. embed_section now uses the helper. A new test covers the reported case. The chatbot also ran a separate comparison on 200000 random pages with no fences and found no difference from the old behaviour.
fixes.words: repowise embed_section heading inside fenced code block markdown section boundary overview_tables.py

fixes.title: orm-lens: objects = models.Manager() is parsed as a model field and drift fails the build
fixes.symptom: A Django model that declares an explicit manager such as objects = models.Manager() gets a field named objects of type Manager. The drift command then reports "declared but never migrated: objects" and exits with code 1 on a healthy project. The ER diagram shows Manager objects as a column.
fixes.change: The fix adds a small set named _NOT_A_FIELD holding Manager and QuerySet in cli/orm_lens/parser.py and skips those assignments including calls that span several lines. TaggableManager stays a relation. The same change is mirrored in the TypeScript parser src/parser.ts. The stored snapshot saleor.snapshot.json loses its one Manager entry. New tests cover the parser and the drift command. A changelog line is included.
fixes.note: Fix 8 and fix 9 both add text at the same spot in CHANGELOG.md. Applying both needs a small manual merge of CHANGELOG.md.
fixes.words: orm-lens drift declared but never migrated: objects models.Manager() parsed as a field Manager objects ER diagram blocking exit code 1 Django
fixes.report_title: drift fails the build on `objects = models.Manager()`: a manager is parsed as a model field

fixes.title: orm-lens: @receiver with a list or tuple of signals becomes one unknown custom edge
fixes.symptom: Django's receiver() accepts one signal or a list or tuple of signals. For @receiver([post_save, post_delete], sender=Attachment) the signals command records a single edge with the signal name `<unknown>` and labels the edge custom. The cascade command then leaves list-form post_delete receivers out of its warning about receivers that will not run for DB_CASCADE rows.
fixes.change: The fix replaces _signal_arg_name with _signal_arg_names in cli/orm_lens/signals_parser.py. The new helper returns one name per signal for a single signal or a list or a tuple. signal_graph adds one edge per name and keeps `<unknown>` only when nothing is readable. New tests cover the list form and the tuple form and the cascade warning. A changelog line is included. The chatbot checked the helper logic with a separate script on seven cases.
fixes.note: Fix 8 and fix 9 both add text at the same spot in CHANGELOG.md. Applying both needs a small manual merge of CHANGELOG.md.
fixes.words: orm-lens signals @receiver([post_save, post_delete]) list tuple of signals `<unknown>` custom edge skipped_receivers DB_CASCADE signal_graph Django
fixes.report_title: signals: @receiver([post_save, post_delete], ...) becomes one '<unknown>' custom edge

fixes.title: Gulliver: check accepts a negative --min-rows and a negative or NaN or infinite --max-change
fixes.symptom: The command gulliver check accepts --min-rows -5 and the check can then never fail. --max-change -5 always fails even when the row count did not change. --max-change nan can never fail.
fixes.change: parse_spec in src/gulliver/checks.py now raises ValueError for a negative min_rows and for a max_change_pct that is negative or NaN or infinite. The check command turns the error into status error with exit code 1 before any query runs. Zero stays valid for both. New tests go through parse_spec and through the command line. A changelog line is included.
fixes.words: gulliver check --min-rows negative --max-change nan inf parse_spec CheckSpec threshold validation
fixes.note: Fix 10 and fix 21 both add text at the same spots in CHANGELOG.md and tests/test_cli_and_mcp.py. Applying both needs a small manual merge.
fixes.report_title: check: refuse a negative --min-rows and a negative, NaN or infinite --max-change

fixes.title: wheelgap: a private-index lockfile package with no file list is still looked up on PyPI
fixes.symptom: An old-format poetry.lock records hashes under [metadata.hashes] and gives packages no file list. A package from a private index in such a lock file is looked up on pypi.org by name. The internal package name gets sent to a public server and a public package with the same name can be reported in place of the internal one.
fixes.change: fill_all in src/wheelgap/pypi.py now marks a package with no files and a non-PyPI registry as skipped with the reason private index before any lookup. The --offline check in src/wheelgap/cli.py no longer counts such a package as needing the index. A PyPI package with no file list is still looked up. One existing test that asserted the old behaviour is replaced. New tests cover the function and the command line. A changelog line is included.
fixes.note: The --offline change goes one step beyond the bug report text. A maintainer may prefer to drop that one line.
fixes.words: wheelgap poetry.lock metadata.hashes private index dependency confusion fill_all PyPI lookup skipped private index
fixes.report_title: Lockfiles: a private-index package with no file list is still looked up on PyPI

fixes.title: repowise: test_tool_overview.py fails when run alone because ov.health does not exist yet
fixes.symptom: Running tests/unit/server/mcp/test_tool_overview.py alone fails with AttributeError: module 'repowise.server.mcp_server.tool_overview' has no attribute 'health'. The package loads its submodules lazily so ov.health only exists after another test imports the submodule.
fixes.change: The test now imports repowise.server.mcp_server.tool_overview.health itself and patches _get_health_metrics on that module. One test changed. No product code changed.
fixes.note: The bug report already had one comment on 9 November 2026 and the chatbot could not read comments. Someone may already be working on the bug report.
fixes.words: repowise test_tool_overview AttributeError has no attribute health lazy_exports monkeypatch test order dependent
fixes.report_title: [Bug] test_tool_overview.py fails when run on its own because `ov.health` only exists after another test imports it

fixes.title: rai-toolkit: malformed JSON dataset errors do not name the file
fixes.symptom: DatasetLoader.from_file() names the source file when a JSON dataset has the wrong shape. For malformed JSON the loader lets a bare JSONDecodeError through such as "Expecting ',' delimiter: line 3 column 3 (char 26)" with no file name. Failures are hard to trace when several datasets are loaded.
fixes.change: DatasetLoader._load_json in rai_toolkit/evaluation/datasets.py now catches json.JSONDecodeError and raises ValueError with the path and the one-based line and column and the parser's short reason. The original error is kept as the cause. No dataset content appears in the message. New tests cover a direct array and a data wrapper and an empty file and two kinds of truncated JSON. The chatbot checked the expected line and column numbers with a separate script.
fixes.note: The bug report asks contributors to check linked pull requests first. The chatbot could not see linked pull requests.
fixes.words: rai-toolkit DatasetLoader from_file JSONDecodeError Expecting delimiter missing filename path line column invalid JSON
fixes.report_title: fix(datasets): include source paths in JSON syntax errors

fixes.title: inspect_scout: retry_refusals=True allows one retry instead of the default three
fixes.symptom: llm_scanner(retry_refusals=True) gives up after two refused responses and raises RefusalError. retry_refusals=3 recovers. The option accepts a bool or an int and Python treats True as the integer 1 so the branch that maps True to 3 never runs.
fixes.change: The resolution code in src/inspect_scout/_llm_scanner/_llm_scanner.py now checks for a bool before an int. True means 3 retries and False means 0 and an explicit integer keeps its meaning. The docstring says so. A new test passes retry_refusals=True with three refusals followed by a success.
fixes.note: The person who reported the bug offered to prepare a fix. Please check the bug report for a linked pull request before sending this one. The project builds its changelog automatically so the patch adds no changelog line.
fixes.words: inspect_scout llm_scanner retry_refusals True RefusalError isinstance bool int content_filter one retry instead of three
fixes.report_title: retry_refusals=True allows one retry instead of the default three

fixes.title: audiobard: export_m4b crashes when the destination folder does not exist
fixes.symptom: Running audiobard generate book.txt -o ./new_folder/book.m4b fails with the FFmpeg error "new_folder/book.m4b: No such file or directory". The MP3 export path creates missing folders and the M4B export path does not.
fixes.change: export_m4b in src/audiobard/audio/processor.py now creates the destination folder before calling FFmpeg. A new test exports into a nested folder that does not exist yet. A changelog line is included.
fixes.note: Fix 15 and fix 16 both add text at the same spot in CHANGELOG.md. Applying both needs a small manual merge of CHANGELOG.md.
fixes.words: audiobard export_m4b ffmpeg No such file or directory output folder missing parent directory mkdir m4b
fixes.report_title: [BUG] AudioProcessor.export_m4b crashes if destination parent directory does not exist

fixes.title: audiobard: the Spanish title don matches inside the English contraction don't
fixes.symptom: VoiceMapper guesses the gender of a neutral character from clue words in names and aliases. The male clue list holds the Spanish title don. An apostrophe counts as a word break so the clue also matches inside don't. An alias such as "The girl who don't talk" gets a male voice.
fixes.change: _has_whole_word_clue in src/audiobard/tts/voice_mapper.py no longer counts a clue that is directly followed by an apostrophe and the letter t. Both the plain apostrophe and the curly apostrophe are covered. Other forms such as he's still count. New tests cover the helper and a full voice assignment. A changelog line is included. The chatbot checked the pattern with a separate script on twelve phrases.
fixes.note: Fix 15 and fix 16 both add text at the same spot in CHANGELOG.md. Applying both needs a small manual merge of CHANGELOG.md.
fixes.words: audiobard VoiceMapper gender clue don don't contraction word boundary apostrophe GenderHint MALE wrong voice
fixes.report_title: [BUG] Word-boundary contraction bug in VoiceMapper matches 'don' inside 'don't'

fixes.title: spatialmath-python: InterpSplineSE3 rejects negative start times and mishandles a zero time span
fixes.symptom: InterpSplineSE3([-5, -3, -1], poses) raises ValueError because the constructor tests the last time point instead of the span between the first and the last. A span of zero is not caught and fails later with an unrelated SciPy error when normalize_time is on. The error message prints {self._e} literally because the f prefix is missing.
fixes.change: The constructor in spatialmath/spline.py now checks the last time minus the first time and the message is a real f-string. The two length checks now run before the span check so a single time point still gets the message about needing two data points. New tests cover negative and offset start times with and without normalize_time and a zero span.
fixes.note: The bug report had one comment on 9 November 2026 and the chatbot could not read comments.
fixes.words: spatialmath InterpSplineSE3 negative timepoints ValueError Difference between start and end timepoints is less than {self._e} zero time span normalize_time
fixes.report_title: InterpSplineSE3 rejects negative start times and mishandles a zero time span

fixes.title: huri-modules: test_install.sh reads $target before setting the variable (SC2318)
fixes.symptom: In scripts/test_install.sh the function prepare_workdir declares local target="$1" dir="$WORK_BASE/$target" on one line. Bash expands $target in the second assignment before the first assignment has taken effect. The function works only because the caller's loop variable has the same name. shellcheck reports the line as SC2318.
fixes.change: The fix splits the line into two local statements so dir is built from the function's own target. The chatbot confirmed with bash -n that the script still parses. shellcheck was not available to the chatbot.
fixes.words: huri-modules test_install.sh prepare_workdir SC2318 local target dir same line shellcheck bash
fixes.report_title: test_install.sh: prepare_workdir reads $target before it sets it (SC2318)

fixes.title: huri-modules: RemoteEmbedder ignores --no-verify-ssl and never verifies TLS
fixes.symptom: python -m huri_rag.ingestion has a --no-verify-ssl flag. The flag is honoured for Qdrant. RemoteEmbedder always builds its HTTP client with verify=False so an HTTPS embeddings endpoint is never verified. bandit reports the line as B501.
fixes.change: RemoteEmbedder.__init__ in packages/huri-module-rag/huri_rag/ingestion.py gains a verify_ssl parameter that defaults to True and passes the value to httpx.Client. The script passes its verify_ssl value when building the embedder. A new test file checks that both values reach the client with no network use. The package version goes from 0.1.0 to 0.1.1 and the two matching pins in meta/pyproject.toml follow.
fixes.note: The default behaviour changes: TLS is verified unless --no-verify-ssl is passed. The new test is skipped when the rag extra is not installed.
fixes.words: huri-modules huri_rag ingestion RemoteEmbedder httpx.Client verify=False --no-verify-ssl TLS certificate verification bandit B501
fixes.report_title: RemoteEmbedder ignores --no-verify-ssl and never verifies TLS

fixes.title: agent-blueprint: lint rule unused-produced-field ignores fields read by policies.escalation
fixes.symptom: abp lint warns that a node produces the state field confidence and that nothing consumes the field. The escalation policy reads that field at runtime to decide the route. The warning is a false positive and nudges people to delete a field the escalation guarantee depends on.
fixes.change: The consumed state fields block in src/agent_blueprint/linting.py now counts confidence as consumed when policies.escalation has both on_low_confidence and confidence_threshold set. Those are the same two conditions the generated runtime checks before reading the field. A new test file covers the escalation case and two cases where the warning still fires. A changelog line is included.
fixes.note: The bug report names an example file that is not in the main branch so the chatbot could not check that file. The patch also extends the warning text to mention the escalation policy.
fixes.words: agent-blueprint abp lint unused-produced-field confidence policies.escalation on_low_confidence confidence_threshold false positive
fixes.report_title: lint: unused-produced-field ignores fields read by policies.escalation

fixes.title: Gulliver: inspect quietly clamps --limit and --scan values outside the allowed range
fixes.symptom: gulliver inspect --limit 0 lists 1 table and --limit 500 lists at most 200 and --sensitive --scan 5000 scans 1000 rows and --scan -5 scans nothing. No message tells the person that the number was changed. The MCP tool already refuses the same values.
fixes.change: core.inspect and guard.inspect_sensitive now return status error with a next step for a limit outside 1 to 200 and a scan value outside 0 to 1000. The limit is still ignored when a table is named and --scan 0 still means no value scan. A new test covers the functions and the command line. A changelog line is included.
fixes.note: Fix 10 and fix 21 both add text at the same spots in CHANGELOG.md and tests/test_cli_and_mcp.py. Applying both needs a small manual merge. The bug report had one comment on 9 November 2026 and the chatbot could not read comments.
fixes.words: gulliver inspect --limit --scan clamp silently out of range 1-200 0-1000 inspect_sensitive status error
fixes.report_title: inspect: refuse --limit and --scan outside the range MCP already enforces, instead of quietly clamping

fixes.title: microscopy-active-learning: pretrain trains zero steps when the dataset is smaller than the batch size
fixes.symptom: pretrain and pretrain_crossmodal only run full batches. With fewer images than the batch size the loop body never runs. No optimisation step happens and the function returns a loss history of 0.0 with no error.
fixes.change: A new helper effective_batch in src/maldl/training/contrastive.py clamps the batch size to the dataset size with a warning and raises ValueError for fewer than 2 samples. Both training functions use the helper. New tests check that the encoder weights change and that the loss is above zero and that one sample is refused. The chatbot checked the batch arithmetic with a separate script.
fixes.note: The bug report allowed either clamping with a warning or raising an error. The patch clamps. A batch size below 2 now raises an error too.
fixes.words: microscopy-active-learning maldl pretrain pretrain_crossmodal batch larger than dataset zero steps loss 0.0 contrastive NT-Xent
fixes.report_title: pretrain() silently trains zero steps when the dataset is smaller than the batch size

fixes.title: orm-lens: suggest-indexes proposes an index that already exists when Meta.indexes names the foreign key column
fixes.symptom: A Django foreign key can be named by field (category) or by column (category_id). suggest-indexes compares the two spellings as different text. An index declared with fields category_id and slug is proposed again as category and slug. filter(category_id=x) and filter(category=y) are counted as two different fields.
fixes.change: cli/orm_lens/query_analyzer.py gains helpers that fold a name ending in _id onto the foreign key field name when the model really has that foreign key. The folding is applied to the lookup rows and to the index groups read from Meta. A plain field that only ends in _id keeps its name. New tests cover the three cases from the bug report. A changelog line is included.
fixes.note: Fixes 8 and 9 and 23 all add text at the same spot in CHANGELOG.md. Applying more than one needs a small manual merge of CHANGELOG.md.
fixes.words: orm-lens suggest-indexes Meta.indexes category_id foreign key column alias duplicate index proposal filter(category_id=) Django
fixes.report_title: suggest-indexes proposes an index that exists when Meta.indexes names the FK column (`category_id`)

fixes.title: openmed: drift report compares score histograms that use different bin counts
fixes.symptom: compute_drift_report accepts a reference window with a 10-bin score histogram and an observation window with a 20-bin score histogram. Buckets are named by index so the two windows are compared bucket by bucket as if the buckets meant the same thing. The report then shows drift that is only a change of binning or hides real drift.
fixes.change: compute_drift_report in openmed/eval/drift_monitor.py now raises DriftInputError when the two score histograms differ in length. The message names both lengths and contains no bucket values. The all-zero default histogram follows the same rule. New tests cover matching and mismatched and default histograms. A changelog line is included.
fixes.words: openmed drift_monitor compute_drift_report score_histogram bin count mismatch DriftInputError PSI 10 bins 20 bins
fixes.report_title: Reject drift windows whose score histograms use a different bin count

fixes.title: repo-roast-skill: the Bailiff cannot parse cited paths that contain spaces
fixes.symptom: verdict.py matches evidence such as docs/My Guide.md:12 with a pattern that stops at whitespace. A citation of a real file and line is thrown out as having no evidence when the path contains a space.
fixes.change: skills/roast-repo/verdict.py gains a second pattern for a citation wrapped whole in backticks. Inside backticks the path may contain spaces. Citations without backticks behave as before. The existing check that keeps paths inside the repository still applies. A new test covers paths with spaces and ranges and missing files and paths outside the repository. The chatbot checked both patterns with a separate script on ten phrases.
fixes.note: A path with spaces is accepted only when the whole citation is wrapped in backticks. The bug report named that as the minimum.
fixes.words: repo-roast-skill verdict.py Bailiff LOCATION regex path with spaces evidence path:line backticks
fixes.report_title: Bailiff can't parse cited paths that contain spaces

fixes.title: kitden: add panels show one gap too many above the hint
fixes.symptom: In the Gateway and Library add panels the closed Add a GitHub source block draws nothing but still counts as an item of the panel's column. The block adds one more 12 pixel gap above the hint line.
fixes.change: src/kitden/web/static/style.css gets one rule that hides the block while the block is closed. The Sources control still opens and closes the block. A new test in tests/unit/test_page_words.py pins the rule. ROADMAP.md gets a line under Not released yet.
fixes.note: The bug report asks for the README picture to be made again. The chatbot could not make pictures of the page. The bug report says the maintainer will make the picture in that case.
fixes.words: kitden add panel discovery-source-add details closed extra gap 12px hint Click to review drag onto style.css
fixes.report_title: Add panels: one gap too many above the hint
